title: Chemical Bonding
description: Atoms share electrons because a shared wavefunction has lower energy. Unlocks the Chemical Reactor.

puzzle.goal: Two identical atoms A and B each hold one orbital, φ on A and χ on B. Try the shared trial wave φ + χ and compute its energy as the expectation value of the Hamiltonian H divided by the norm of the trial wave. Using the symmetry of the two atoms, write the energy in terms of the on-site integral ⟨φ|H|φ⟩, the hopping integral ⟨φ|H|χ⟩ and the overlap ⟨φ|χ⟩.
puzzle.name: Bonding-orbital energy of the LCAO (Hückel-type) variational treatment
puzzle.form: ( mel ( φ , H , φ ) + mel ( φ , H , χ ) ) / ( 1 + braket ( φ , χ ) )
puzzle.ask: With α = ⟨φ|H|φ⟩ = −13.6 eV, β = ⟨φ|H|χ⟩ = −10 eV and overlap S = @{S}, find how far the bonding orbital lies below a lone atomic orbital: α − E.
puzzle.method: Expand ⟨φ+χ|H|φ+χ⟩ / ⟨φ+χ|φ+χ⟩; with normalised, identical orbitals the numerator is 2(α+β) and the denominator 2(1+S).
